title: The snail and the cracked tile
prompt:
A snail starts on one tile of a large tiled terrace and must reach the tile 6 tiles to the right of it and 5 tiles up. Each move takes it one tile right or one tile up.

The tile 4 right and 3 up from the start is broken, so the snail never steps on it. How many different paths are there?
hints: A path is a string of right moves and up moves: how many moves does a path to the end have, and how many of them go right?
How many paths are there if no tile is broken?
How many of those paths step on the broken tile, counting the part before it and the part after it?
solution:
**252.**

Count all paths, then take away the ones that step on the broken tile.

Any path is 11 moves, of which 6 are right: C(11, 6) = 462 (choose which moves go right).

Paths through the broken tile: 4 right and 3 up to reach it: C(7, 4) = 35 ways, then 2 right and 2 up from there: C(4, 2) = 6 ways, so 210 in all. The answer is 462 − 210 = **252**.

The common slip is to subtract only the 35 ways of reaching the broken tile, forgetting that each of them can continue to the end in several ways.
